items.stem: A workflow uses ChatGPT to draft and then send customer emails automatically. What control most reduces risk?

options.text: A human approval checkpoint before any email is sent
options.rationale: Correct: a human gate before an irreversible external action limits the impact of errors.
Prompt length does not control an irreversible action.
Model version does not add an approval control.
Raising limits increases, not reduces, risk.

items.explanation: Correct: a human gate before an irreversible external action limits the impact of errors.

items.stem: Which connector configuration best follows least privilege for a summarisation task over one project folder?

options.text: Read-only access scoped to that single folder
options.rationale: Correct: read-only, narrowly scoped access grants only what the task needs.

options.text: Full read-write access to the entire drive
options.rationale: This grants far more than the task requires.

options.text: Admin access to the whole workspace
options.rationale: Workspace admin is grossly over-privileged for summarisation.
Write access is unnecessary and risky for a read task.

items.explanation: Correct: read-only, narrowly scoped access grants only what the task needs.

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce standing risk from connected apps over time? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: monitoring surfaces misuse or anomalies in connected actions.

options.text: Revoke connector access when it is no longer needed
options.rationale: Correct: removing unused access reduces the standing attack surface.

options.text: Grant write access by default to save time
options.rationale: Default write access increases risk and violates least privilege.

items.explanation: Correct: monitoring surfaces misuse or anomalies in connected actions.
